question_text: Find the number of ways of arranging the letters of the word INDEPENDENCE.

mark_split.label: Count the letters and the repeats

recall_prompt: Say how you would count the arrangements of the word INDEPENDENCE — what you count first and which formula you use.
insider_note: Write INDEPENDENCE out and number the letters: 12 in all, with E four times, N three times and D twice. The D pair is the repeat most often missed, and one missed pair doubles the answer.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Count the letters and the repeats
steps.margin_note: First mark. I-N-D-E-P-E-N-D-E-N-C-E: 12 letters. E appears 4 times, N 3 times, D twice; I, P, C once.
steps.memory_tip: Write it out and number: I-N-D-E-P-E-N-D-E-N-C-E. E four times, N three times, D twice.
lines: E four times, N three times, D twice.

recall.must_convey: That INDEPENDENCE has 12 letters with E four times, N three times and D twice.
accept: twelve letters, E four times, N three times, D twice
count the letters, twelve, with four E, three N and two D
the repeats are E four, N three, D two
twelve letters, E nalugu sarlu, N moodu, D rendu
find the repeated letters first, E N and D

steps.why: Alike letters cannot be told apart, so swapping them does not give a new arrangement. The count of each repeated letter is what the formula divides by, so it must be found before anything else.
common_mistakes: Counting E three times instead of four.
Missing that N appears three times (positions 2, 7, 10).

steps.label: Apply n!/(p!·q!·r!)
steps.memory_tip: 12!/(4!·3!·2!) = 16,63,200. Missing the D pair doubles the answer.

recall.must_convey: That the count is 12 factorial over 4 factorial times 3 factorial times 2 factorial.
accept: twelve factorial over four factorial three factorial two factorial
n factorial by p factorial q factorial r factorial, twelve factorial by four factorial three factorial two factorial
divide twelve factorial by two hundred eighty eight
twelve factorial by four factorial into three factorial into two factorial
the answer is twelve factorial over four factorial three factorial two factorial which is sixteen lakh sixty three thousand two hundred

steps.why: n! counts the arrangements as if every letter were different; each group of p alike letters has been counted p! times over, so dividing by p! for each group leaves the true count.
common_mistakes: Dividing by 4!·3! only and forgetting the D pair.
Dividing by 9! (the sum 4 + 3 + 2) instead of the product of factorials.
